text:
Alex P.: Heads-up: I'm about to roll a tightened KMS policy for the keystore service to reduce cross-project decrypt surface. posting the plan here for fast feedback.
Jin T.: paste the policy fragment? want to check resource patterns before you push.
Alex P.: snippet: ```json
{"bindings":[{"role":"roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter","members":["serviceAccount:keystore@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"],"condition":{"expression":"resource.name.startsWith('projects/redwood/locations/*/keyRings/keystore')"}}]}```
Ravi M.: watch out: proxies call Decrypt on cryptoKeyVersion resource paths (they include `/cryptoKeyVersions/1`). startsWith might not match the full resource.name value. recommend using `resource.name.matches()` regex or grant on the cryptoKey resource explicitly.
Alex P.: good catch. We assumed the KMS API normalized names. Is there a safe regex we can use?
Jin T.: try `resource.name.matches('projects/.*/locations/.*/keyRings/keystore/cryptoKeys/.*/cryptoKeyVersions/.*')` or just grant on `projects/redwood/locations/*/keyRings/keystore/cryptoKeys/*`. simpler and auditable.
ops-bot: ALERT: 2850013390 - KMS.DecryptAccessDenied spike detected in ap-southeast-1 (12 fails / 3m).
Nia H.: seeing increased TLS handshake failures on the ap-southeast edge fleet since 09:12: logs show "failed to unwrap private key: KMS.DecryptAccessDenied".
Alex P.: that was within the rollout window (09:10). rolling back now if we confirm.
Ravi M.: before rollback, can we validate which resource string triggered the deny? use audit logs filter: `protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" AND protoPayload.status.code=7 AND resource.labels.location="ap-southeast-1"`.
Jin T.: ran that query and pasted two samples: the resource in protoPayload.resourceName is `projects/redwood/locations/ap-southeast-1/cryptoKeyVersions/1` (missing keyRing/cryptoKey segments in the logged name). that's what breaks our startsWith check.
Alex P.: okay immediate action: re-grant decrypt with a time-bounded emergency binding to prevent outages. I'll add a condition on request.time < timestamp("2026-06-15T09:40:00Z") so it auto-expiries.
ops-bot: SUGGESTION: use audit-runbook entry "kms-decrypt-deny" to auto-collect logs and link cert rotation jobs.
Nia H.: also throttle keystore unwrap retries on proxies for canary regions to avoid stampeding failures. current backoff is aggressive.
Ravi M.: root cause summary: IAM condition pattern didn't match the protoPayload.resourceName format emitted by the KMS API in this region; some SDKs/clients call the Decrypt RPC referencing the version resource directly. fix = adjust condition or bind to key resources explicitly.
Alex P.: rollback applied at 09:24 UTC. monitoring.
ops-bot: UPDATE: 2850014400 - KMS.DecryptAccessDenied reduced to 0 in ap-southeast-1 after rollback.
Jin T.: validating TLS now. probe command: `openssl s_client -connect edge.ap-southeast-1.redwood.com:443 -cert test.pem -key test.key -tls1_3` returned successful handshake and cert chain.
Nia H.: cert-rot job in eu-central queued failed earlier; paused all scheduled rotations until we validate policy templates.
Alex P.: follow-ups: 1) publish policy template that uses explicit cryptoKey resource names and a regex for versions, 2) add unit tests that simulate Decrypt proto resourceName formats, 3) update canary docs to run KMS audit query before rotating certs in a region, 4) reduce keystore retry aggressiveness for new deployments.
Ravi M.: I'll file an incident note and include the audit query + sample denies and a small snippet for the regex-based policy.
Jin T.: propose a short postmortem meeting tomorrow to lock the policy pattern and review the console alerts thresholds.
Alex P.: thanks all. keeping rotations paused until templates land. I'll link the incident ticket to this thread. :white_check_mark:
